verdict.rationale: Bugbot is itself an AI reviewer you can hand work to. On request, a user can comment `cursor review` or `bugbot run` on a PR, and it reviews in the background, posting findings with suggested fixes. The delegable task is limited to code review, though: actually applying fixes hands off to the separate Cursor IDE or cursor.com/agents via 'Fix in Cursor' / 'Fix in Web' links, and that is not credited here. Missing for 10: delegation of arbitrary tasks beyond review, a conversational assistant interface within Bugbot, and independent hands-on evidence of delegation workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Manual trigger by commenting `cursor review` or `bugbot run` on any PR
When enabled, Bugbot automatically runs AI code review in the background on new PRs.
It analyzes every pull request for bugs, security vulnerabilities, and code quality issues, leaving inline comments with explanations and suggested fixes.
